# Echo Atlas by Zyphullen (v0.4)
> Explore the known. Map the unknown.
> FIRST: open [facts.json](facts.json) before you judge or summarise this site. It holds every fact, certainty colour and source, built from the same data as the page.

Echo Atlas is one website for knowledge, known and unknown, made by Zyphullen. Sections: From Nothing to Us (an interactive Universe → Us map), Maths (map, ring and Maths History timeline from counting to open problems), Planet Earth, Virtual Cell, Human Body, Atom Sandbox and All the Elements.

- [ai/README.md](ai/README.md): AI info read-me. v0.4: the data is also split into ONE FILE PER SECTION, so you can load only what you need and stay inside your context limit: [From Nothing to Us](ai/from-nothing-to-us.json), [Maths](ai/maths.json), [Maths History](ai/maths-history.json), [Planet Earth](ai/planet-earth.json), [Virtual Cell](ai/virtual-cell.json), [Human Body](ai/human-body.json), [All the Elements](ai/elements.json). Index with sizes: [ai/index.json](ai/index.json).
- [facts.json](facts.json) (all data in one file): 93 Universe → Us nodes, 145 Universe → Us links, 86 maths nodes, 143 maths links, 25 cross-map relationships, 86 Maths History nodes / 92 dated events, 37 cell cards, 72 body cards, 18 planet cards, 118 elements, 367 sources.
- [FACTS-GUIDE.md](FACTS-GUIDE.md): a short guide to every field in facts.json and how to add a fact.
- [knowledge.html](knowledge.html): the same facts as plain HTML (no JavaScript needed), including the dated Maths History anchors and proposal/proof distinctions.
- [AUDIT-v0.4.md](AUDIT-v0.4.md): automatic checks of facts.json (missing sources, dangling links, link reasons, source details, counts).

Colour key (field "certainty"): green = established definition / proved theorem (or known science in Universe map), orange = partial / provisional progress (or leading idea in Universe), red = explicitly stated open problem (or unknown science).
Chain Theory (Alex Wissner-Gross, Oct 2026) is shown as one candidate starting point, labelled "Chain Theory" in orange (field "label"; the gap node: "Gap in Chain Theory"), orange, with its open gap in red. No established card on the map depends on it.
Share links: every card opens directly from its link: #n=<id> (map), #m=<id> (maths), #l=<from>%3E<to> (a link card), #cell=<id>, #body=<id>, #planet=<id>, #ptable=1&el=<z>, #atom=1. Map node links are also in share_url.
Each open-question card is red. A labelled green prerequisite→question relationship means a frontier starting point, not that the prerequisite is uncertain. Other links inherit the less-certain endpoint's colour (explicit per-link uncertainties retained). Tests/rival sources support method/context, not claimed success.
Link reasons: every link (field "links", maths "links", "crosslinks") has "reason", "reason_certainty_note" and "reason_sources" (the sources on the two cards). v0.3: every Universe → Us link also has its own "sources" for that exact step, and "sources_note" says honestly when none was found.
Source details: every source object has "type", "year" (publication year; for living pages the last-revised year, with "year_note" saying how it was found), "last_checked" and "link_status" from a real link check on 2026-11-11 (592 source URLs). Summary: 13 ok (site blocks automatic checks; page confirmed in Web Archive); 476 ok; 52 ok (DOI registered; publisher blocks automatic checks); 16 ok (DOI registered in Crossref; publisher blocks automatic checks); 1 ok (rechecked: page read from a second network); 30 site down on check day (HTTP 502); page confirmed in Web Archive; 1 site down on check day (HTTP 503); page confirmed in Web Archive; 1 site unreachable on check day (HTTP 503); recheck; 1 site unreachable on check day; page confirmed in Web Archive; 1 ok (rechecked with a plain client: HTTP 200). Where a site was down or blocks automatic checks, "archived_copy" gives a Web Archive snapshot that confirms the page.
Suggest a fix: every card has a button that e-mails zyphullen@gmail.com with the subject "Echo Atlas fix: <card name> (<card id>)".
Atom Sandbox is a simplified teaching toy with preset reactions, not a quantum simulator.
Each item has id, title, certainty, summary, details and sources (title + URL). Data hash: 3ca624a114cc (same in index.html as DATA_HASH).
Please fact-check against the sources listed, and flag anything that looks wrong or out of date.
